get.description:
Returns list of general ledger events (aka voucher rows).

 ### Pagination ###
 This endpoint supports pagination through the use of **pageIndex** and **pageSize** values in the query parameters. 
 A typical use case is when you have a large number of events, and you want to retrieve them systematically. 
 By specifying the **pageIndex** and **pageSize** values, you can retrieve the dimensions in manageable pages.       
 In the response, you will get pagination metadata to help you figure out the total size of the dataset
 #### Here's an example of using pagination ####
 Suppose you have a total of 100 events in the system, and you want to retrieve all of them systematically:
* First, make the request with **pageIndex**: 0 and **pageSize**: 50. You will get the first 50 records
* Next, you make the next request with **pageIndex**: 50 and **pageSize**: 50 and you will get the next set of records
* Just to make sure that there is no more records left, make another request with **pageIndex**: 100 and **pageSize**: 50, when there is no more records to show, you will get empty array []

parameters.name: pageIndex
parameters.description: Page index starting from zero.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Amount of the rows returned in single request, maximum is 10000

parameters.description: Start date to fetch vouchers from (inclusive).

get.description:
Retrieves a list of vouchers based on various search criteria. 
It supports pagination and allows filtering by voucher ID, date range, category, and state. 
Additionally, it can include or exclude postings associated with each voucher.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The id parameter is an array of strings that specifies the unique identifiers of the vouchers to be included in the search results. 
            This parameter allows you to filter the vouchers based on their specific IDs.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description:
The dateFrom parameter specifies the minimum date for the voucher date range. 
            It is used to filter vouchers that have a date on or after the specified dateFrom value.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description:
The dateTo parameter specifies the maximum date for the voucher date range. 
            It is used to filter vouchers that have a date on or before the specified dateTo value.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description:
The category parameter is an array of strings that specifies the categories of the vouchers to be included in the search results. 
            This parameter allows you to filter the vouchers based on their assigned categories, such as:
            ePurchaseInvoice, PurchaseInvoice, TravelExpense, eSalesInvoice, SalesInvoice, eSalesInvoiceReceivable, eSalesMemo, Cash, Salary, OnBehalfPaidExpenses,
            CreditCardVouchers, Receipts, Memo, TaxSummary, Other, BankTransactions, ReferenceTransactions, Periodic, History, Concern, VatPostings, Recurrent,
            TaxPeriodisation, MarginalTax, IntegrationSales, IntegrationPurchase, IntegrationSalary, IntegrationMemo, IntegrationBank and IntegrationPeriodic.

parameters.name: voucherState
parameters.description:
The voucherState parameter is an array of strings that specifies the states of the vouchers to be included in the search results. 
            This parameter allows you to filter the vouchers based on their current state, such as "Draft", "Accepted", "Locked", or "Deleted".

parameters.name: pageIndex
parameters.description:
The pageIndex parameter indicates the zero-based index of the page to be returned. 
            Pagination is a common technique used to divide a large dataset into smaller, more manageable chunks or "pages". 
            By specifying the pageIndex, you can retrieve a specific subset of the total results.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
The pageSize parameter determines the number of vouchers to be returned in a single page of results. 
            Pagination is a technique used to divide a large dataset into smaller, more manageable chunks or "pages". 
            By specifying the pageSize, you can control the number of items that are retrieved in each page.

parameters.name: includePostings
parameters.description:
The includePostings parameter is a boolean flag that indicates whether the postings related to 
            each voucher should be included in the response. Postings are typically detailed entries or transactions associated with a voucher, 
            and including them can provide more comprehensive information about each voucher.

post.summary: Add Collection Of Accepted Vouchers V1
post.description:
Adds a collection of accepted vouchers to bookkeeping.

### Voucher ###

A voucher is an object that groups postings with the same category, date, and voucher number.
Typical categories are, for example: IntegrationSales, IntegrationPurchase, and IntegrationSalary.
The voucher date needs to belong to an existing accounting period, and the associated bookkeeping period needs to be open.
A single voucher contains postings which include details such as vatIncludedAmount, vatAmount, and description for specific posting "row".
An acceptor can be a full name or an email address. Each voucher can have only one voucher image but multiple attachments.


### Acceptor ###

The Acceptor typically refers to an individual who holds the responsibility for ensuring the accuracy and correctness of the data recorded in a specific voucher.
In cases where automated accounting processes are employed, the Acceptor may denote the name of the system or software entity that submitted the voucher collection.
Accepted vouchers should have at least two postings with valid account numbers, and the total of amounts should be zero.
If a voucher is posted as Accepted and if it doesn't meet all requirements, an HTTP 400 Bad Request with a validation error message will be returned.

### Postings ###

A posting has attributes such as an account number, a description, an amount, a matchkey, and dimension values (costCenter, costType, project, projectType).
Account numbers are based on the active chart of accounts. The account should exist and be enabled.
The amounts are based on the default accounting currency for the current region.

By default, the Matchkey field should be left as null.
Matchkeys are essential for creating new ledger items and tracking corresponding matches to existing ledger items.
Matchkeys can be assigned when the posting's account number is a ledger account, and if not provided, the system will generate a new matchkey for ledger account postings.
If mandatory dimensions have been enabled, then the dimension values should be set for each posting with a profit account.

### Voucher image ###

The voucher image must always be in PDF format and serialized as a base64 string. You can include the image in the JSON body using the 'VoucherImageBase64Str' field.

### Performance aspects ###

The number of vouchers in a collection should be based on the number of postings and matchkeys.
The more items or matchkeys there are, the longer the process will take.

### Example request - Bare minimum Accepted state voucher ###

```json
[{
	"category": "Cash",
	"voucherDate": "2023-10-31",      
	"description": "Sales October",     
	"postings": [
		{        
			"accountNumber": "3000",        
			"description": "Buckets",
			"vatIncludedAmount": -2300.00
		},
		{
			"accountNumber": "2365",
			"vatIncludedAmount": 2300
		}
	],        
	"acceptor": "John Doe"        
}]        
```

### Example response - GUID for the created voucher ###

```json
[
  {
    "voucherId": "e2bc83d3-0d9b-4f46-5ee6-08dbd9ed91c1"
  }
]
```

post.description:
Detailed version of voucher collection posting.

 ### Voucher ###
 
 A voucher is an object that groups postings with the same category, date, and voucher number.
 Typical categories include, for example: eSalesInvoice, ePurchaseInvoice, Memo, and BankTransaction.
 The voucher date must belong to an existing accounting period, and the associated bookkeeping period
 must be open.
 Vouchers also have attributes such as an invoice number, a reference number, a concern number, and an acceptor.
 Reference numbers can be used to match vouchers if the information is provided and if matchkeys are undefined.
 An acceptor can be a full name or an email address.
 Each voucher can have only one voucher image but multiple attachments.
 Different validation rules are applied based on the voucher states:
 * Draft vouchers are pending for acceptance. By default, the vouchers will be candidates for automated handling (fetching voucher details, running posting rules, running AI, etc.)
 * Accepted vouchers should have at least two postings with valid account numbers, and the total of
 amounts should be zero.
 * Locked vouchers are read-only protected. This state is set when the associated bookkeeping period is closed.
 
 Vouchers can be posted in Draft, Accepted, or Locked states.
 A voucher remains in a Draft state until it fulfills all the prerequisites for transitioning to the Accepted state, at which point it can be accepted either automatically by the system or manually by a user.
 If a voucher is posted as Accepted or Locked and it does not meet all Accepted/Locked requirements, an HTTP 400 Bad Request with a
 validation error message will be returned.
 
 ### TryAccept ###
 TryAccept in the JSON body is a feature that can be used for vouchers posted in the Draft state. With TryAccept set as true, the system will attempt to accept the voucher. If the voucher is valid for
 the Accepted state, it will be saved as Accepted, otherwise as Draft.
 
 ### Acceptor ###
 
 The Acceptor typically refers to an individual who holds the responsibility for ensuring the accuracy and correctness of the data recorded in a specific voucher.
 In cases where automated accounting processes are employed, the Acceptor may denote the name of the system or software entity that submitted the voucher collection.
 
 ### Postings ###
 
 A posting has attributes such as an account number, a description, an amount, a matchkey, and dimension values (costCenter, costType, project, projectType).
 Account numbers are based on the active chart of accounts. The account should exist and be enabled.
 The amounts are based on the default accounting currency for the current region.
 
 By default, the Matchkey field should be left as null.
 Matchkeys are essential for creating new ledger items and tracking corresponding matches to existing ledger items.
 Matchkeys can be assigned when the posting's account number is a ledger account, and if not provided, the system will generate a new matchkey for ledger account postings.
 If mandatory dimensions have been enabled, then the dimension values should be set for each posting with a profit account.
 
 ### Voucher image ###
 
 The voucher image must always be in PDF format and serialized as a base64 string. You can include the image in the JSON body using the 'VoucherImageBase64Str' field.
 
 ### Voucher details ###
 
 Voucher details can be provided to facilitate voucher automation and to provide more detailed information for the accountant.
 The more details provided, the more likely the voucher will be processed and accepted automatically.


 ### Performance aspects ###
 
 The number of vouchers in a collection should be based on the number of postings and matchkeys.
 The more items or matchkeys there are, the longer the process will take.
 
 ### Example request - Bare minimum Accepted state voucher ###
 
	[{
		"category": "Cash",
		"voucherState": "Accepted",
		"voucherDate": "2023-10-31",      
		"description": "Sales October",     
		"vatIncludedAmount": 2300.00,
		"postings": [
			{        
				"accountNumber": "3000",        
				"description": "Buckets",
				"vatIncludedAmount": -2300.00
			},
			{
				"accountNumber": "2365",
				"vatIncludedAmount": 2300
			}
		],        
		"acceptor": "John Doe"        
	}]        
	
	
 ### Example request - Bare minimum Draft voucher ###
	[{
		"category": "TravelExpense",
		"description": "Destination",
		"voucherState": "Draft",
		"postings": [
			{                
				"vatIncludedAmount": -500.00
			},
			{        
				"vatIncludedAmount": 500.00
			}
		]        
	}]
	
 ### Example response - GUID for the created voucher ###
 
 [
   {
     "voucherId": "e2bc83d3-0d9b-4f46-5ee6-08dbd9ed91c1"
   }
 ]
